transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (CTO, SummitAI), Lena Ruiz (Sr ML Engineer), Omar Khan (Infra), Rita (note taker)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, I'm Alex from Redwood, and this is Priya, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Michael Torres: good, thanks for setting this up, we've been looking at Redwood for a couple weeks, excited to learn how Dedicated could map to our needs.
[00:12] Priya Patel: awesome, yeah, today we'd love to hear about your current infra, traffic patterns, models, and the must-have security requirements so we can map Dedicated recommendations.
[00:22] Lena Ruiz: quick context - SummitAI runs a set of transformer models for real-time summarization and entity extraction. about 300qps on average for the last month, but we've big spikes during product launch events 3-4x baseline. latency SLO is 150ms p50 for the smaller model and p95 under 500ms.
[00:40] Omar Khan: infra-wise we're on AWS, mixing EC2 for app tier and GKE for ML infra. we prefer VPC peering or private link rather than public internet. also we have a managed KMS for key rotation, and audit logs are a must.
[00:57] Alex Chen: great - sounds like classic Dedicated fit. quick clarification - when you say 300qps, is that simultaneous requests or inference calls per second? and what's your average token length?
[01:07] Lena Ruiz: that's inference calls per second. most requests are short - 64 to 128 tokens output, inputs are ~40 tokens. Occasionally we have longer flows for summarization up to 600 tokens but those are rare (less than 5%).
[01:24] Michael Torres: our main question is isolation. we can't have model artifacts or logs leak to other tenants. we looked at Hosted but worried about noisy neighbors and egress controls.
[01:35] Priya Patel: totally valid. Dedicated provides tenant-isolated GPU pools, network isolation via VPC peering or PrivateLink, and you control key management; we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. logs/audit can be delivered to your S3 or logging endpoint - configurable retention.
[01:53] Michael Torres: do you have SOC 2 or ISO certs? our security team will ask.
[01:58] Alex Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have an ISO readiness pack; for Private deployments we support air-gapped installs, but for Dedicated we offer private control plane with customer-managed VPC. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:16] Omar Khan: great. on capacity booking - how does Reserved vs Burst work? If we commit to N GPUs, can we burst beyond that during peak? and what's pricing like?
[02:26] Priya Patel: good Q. Dedicated capacity is based on reserved GPU pools (e.g., 8x A100s); you pay a baseline reserved price for steady-state. We offer burst capacity on shared clusters or on-demand instances subject to availability - there are policies for burst caps. Typical pattern: reserve for p95 baseline, allow burst up to 2-3x for planned events. Pricing for reserved + burst differs; I'll send an example SKUs/pricing sheet.
[02:49] Michael Torres: what about model compatibility and quantization - we use a custom finetuned Llama variant and are interested in int8 quantized inference to save cost.
[02:58] Priya Patel: we support popular open models and custom model onboarding. the runtime supports quantization-friendly paths and int8/4 for supported architectures. For custom models we do a model onboarding + quick perf validation - part of the pilot. there can be small quality/regression risks with aggressive quant; we recommend running quality checks tied to your eval set during pilot.
[03:21] Lena Ruiz: how's latency guaranteed with batching and KV cache? our workflows are sensitive to p50.
[03:27] Priya Patel: the runtime does continuous batching but with latency SLO hooks; you can pin routes to low-latency nodes with small batch windows. KV cache helps for multi-turn chat; for short single-shot inference you get minimal cache benefit. We can configure per-route latency targets and route to dedicated low-latency pools.
[03:48] Michael Torres: any gotchas with our VPC? we have strict egress rules and only certain outbound endpoints allowed.
[03:55] Alex Chen: we can peer via VPC peering or PrivateLink. For tight egress controls, we can deploy a private control plane and keep all traffic in your VPC; that is more like our Private product, but Dedicated can be configured to minimize egress and use customer-managed endpoints. We'll need your network diagram to confirm.
[04:12] Omar Khan: ok we'll share network diagrams and a list of allowed endpoints - expect that in the next few days.
[04:18] Priya Patel: perfect. can you talk about your success criteria for the pilot? what metrics will determine if Dedicated is a fit?
[04:25] Michael Torres: three things - latency under target at peak, cost per 1M tokens better than our current EC2 fleet after accounting for ops, and no gaps in compliance (audit logs + KMS). If those are green we'll consider a 12-month reserved commit.
[04:43] Alex Chen: that aligns with what other customers do. For cost we'll provide TCO examples: reserved baseline + burst vs self-hosted EC2 with ops overhead. We'll also run benchmarks with your prompt set.
[04:55] Lena Ruiz: on benchmarks - how invasive are they? can we run them with anonymized data?
[05:00] Priya Patel: yes, anonymized prompts are fine. We usually ask for a representative prompt set and expected percentiles. We'll run latency and throughput tests, and share raw traces and perf dashboards.
[05:12] Michael Torres: who will execute the benchmark? do we need to give you access to our infra?
[05:16] Priya Patel: We can run tests from Redwood side against a sandbox endpoint in your VPC, or provide a runbook and you can run them internally with the same results. For sensitive infra, customers prefer to run locally and share results.
[05:30] Michael Torres: ok, we'll decide which path.
[05:33] Omar Khan: two infra constraints: 1) all egress must go through our firewall with TLS inspection, 2) we have an internal HSM and require KMS integration for model encryption keys. can Redwood integrate with external HSM?
[05:45] Alex Chen: yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and we can integrate with external HSMs via standard APIs (KMIP/Cloud KMS connectors). We'll include integration notes in the security doc.
[05:56] Lena Ruiz: On model updates - we have frequent model retrains (weekly). What's the model rollout story? can you support canary rollouts and A/B tests?
[06:04] Priya Patel: yes. Dedicated supports rollouts: canary deploys, percent-based traffic splits, and automatic fallback to previous versions on regressions. We also expose trace hooks so you can link model outputs to evals.
[06:18] Michael Torres: what about observability - can we see per-route token cost and latency?
[06:23] Alex Chen: Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost, per-route latency heatmaps, and trace links to prompts. For Dedicated we can also give you access to per-node metrics if needed.
[06:33] Michael Torres: competitive question - we've also evaluated Anthropic and Replicate. Replicate is cheaper for some workloads but we worry about enterprise controls. Thoughts?
[06:42] Alex Chen: Anthropic has good models but enterprise feature parity varies; Replicate is flexible but not always optimized for high-throughput low-latency production setups. Redwood focuses on predictable economics and operational tooling - that's our differentiation.
[06:55] Lena Ruiz: timeline - we'd like to start a pilot in early August if possible.
[06:59] Alex Chen: sounds doable. typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: onboarding, model validation, benchmark runs, and a short evaluation. We'll align on scope today.
[07:10] Priya Patel: to scoping - what models do you want to validate in the pilot, and how many endpoints?
[07:15] Michael Torres: start with our summarization model (ft-llama-v2-7b) and a lighter intent classifier. two endpoints, target baseline throughput ~300 qps combined, and ability to burst to ~900 qps for a 2-hour launch window.
[07:33] Priya Patel: good. we'll size reserved GPUs to handle p95 baseline with headroom; then configure burst policy for the 2-hour event. Typically we'd recommend reserving for p95 baseline - that might be 4-8 A100s depending on model quantization. we'll run perf to refine.
[07:52] Omar Khan: billing question - if we reserve capacity but don't use it during off-months, is there credit or rolling commit?
[07:58] Alex Chen: reserved contracts are monthly or annual; there is usually a term and commit level. For most customers we structure the commit to match average usage and use burst for peaks. We can discuss flexible commit terms with your finance team.
[08:12] Michael Torres: legal/compliance - will we need a Data Processing Agreement and standard terms?
[08:17] Alex Chen: yes, we'll provide DPAs and security addenda. For larger customers we have enterprise agreements. We'll loop in Legal as needed.
[08:26] Lena Ruiz: anything else about reliability? how do you handle instance failures during a high-burst event?
[08:31] Priya Patel: the runtime supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants and cross-pool failover. For Dedicated we also offer SLA-backed uptime targets as part of committed contracts.
[08:43] Michael Torres: okay, that helps.
[08:45] Alex Chen: quick recap and next steps - we'll: 1) send pricing + Dedicated SKUs, 2) share security pack and KMS/HSM integration notes, 3) share benchmark runbook and ask for a prompt set, 4) get network diagram from Omar, and 5) tentatively schedule pilot kickoff for week of Aug 9. Does that capture everything?
[09:03] Michael Torres: yes. please include example reserved sizing so we can review with finance.
[09:08] Alex Chen: will do. Anything else from SummitAI?
[09:11] Lena Ruiz: no, thanks.
[09:12] Omar Khan: we'll follow up with the network diagram and allowed endpoints.
[09:15] Alex Chen: great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the docs and next steps.
[09:19] (multiple people): thanks, bye.
